title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1986 axiomatic 'analysis situs' (second draft). In it a 'figure' F is an object with a set of strata F~. Among all possible strata is a distinguished class L of 'lieux' (loci). These appear to be the minimal or point-like strata. There are also relations of disjointness (||), refinement (<<), and 'shadow' ombr(F).

This page introduces discrete figures.

Definition: a figure Φ is discrete if all its strata are lieux, i.e. Φ~ ⊂ L.

Corollary: a discrete figure is determined by the subset A = Φ~ of L. This A consists of pairwise disjoint lieux. Conversely, a finite subset A ⊂ L 'is' (defines) a figure if and only if its elements are pairwise disjoint. So Φ ↦ Φ~ is a bijection between finite discrete figures and finite sets of pairwise disjoint lieux.

The partly crossed-out lines then note what happens when infinite figures are admitted. The same holds there, and arbitrary discrete figures correspond to suitable arbitrary subsets. The remark 'c'est ainsi dans L!' points to the discreteness, or disjointness, being already built into L.

Finally he announces the relative problem: for a given figure F, describe its discrete sub-figures. These are given by certain subsets A ⊂ L. The next page (Cor. 4) characterises them: A ⊂ ombr(F), and for each stratum X of F, A ∩ ombr(X) is a figure, e.g. finite and pairwise disjoint. This is a local-finiteness condition.

Purpose: discrete sub-figures serve as test objects. Cor. 5 on the next page uses them to show that a proper sub-figure G of F misses some lieu x in the shadow of F. They also feed the disjointness and position criteria At 9 / At 10. In modern terms this is the 0-dimensional, locally finite part of a theory of finite or tame stratified spaces.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The passage on infinite (non-finite) figures is heavily corrected and its exact claim is unclear. As stated ('figures quelconques correspondent aux parties quelconques'), it would need a local-finiteness proviso, which Cor. 4 on the next page supplies.

ideas.what: Discrete figure: a figure all of whose strata are lieux; it is equivalent to a set of pairwise disjoint lieux.
ideas.modern_name: 0-dimensional (discrete) stratified subspace / discrete closed subset in a tame or o-minimal stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (stratification theory; o-minimal geometry, van den Dries et al.)
ideas.where_published: The general programme of tame topology is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5, but not this axiomatic detail.

ideas.what: Discrete sub-figures of a figure F are described by subsets A of L lying in the shadow of F and locally finite on each stratum.
ideas.modern_name: locally finite discrete subsets of a stratified space

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine definitional step inside Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic tame-topology draft. It is mildly interesting only as part of that little-known axiomatics; the content itself is elementary.
transcription_corrections: The margin heading below 'discrète' reads 'Corollaire' (underlined, partly overwritten), as given. The struck word at the top-left before 'Définition' is illegible ('Ch.4' is doubtful).
'il (f. et s.) qu'elle soit formée de lieux deux à deux disjoints' — 'f. et s.' (faut et suffit) is correct.
The line 'discrète (c'est ainsi dans L !)' seems to read 'discrète (c'est ainsi aussi dans L !)'.
The crossed lines 'point ... intérieur' and 'Notons que la relation ...' are struck through in the image. The struck word before 'quelconques' in the last paragraph is 'Ae' (a false start for 'A').
Next page: 'lignes deux à deux disjointes' is probably 'lieux deux à deux disjoints', and 'L' is the set of lieux.
